errors.removedErrorIdentity: The original D239 row-count mismatch: printed 23 versus body 24.

guards.fact: Only thin bands with height below 0.4 * typical_h and outside the existing top-edge-border exclusion enter this retention decision.

Qualifying connected-component bounds require height >= 0.25 * typical_h, width >= 0.2 * typical_h and height >= 0.35 * width. Because the enclosing band is thin, component height is also < 0.4 * typical_h and width is implicitly < (0.4 / 0.35) * typical_h; the components are bounded rather than arbitrary long rules.
The pre-existing very-short-number branch is separate. The affected wider-band branch explicitly requires at least three qualifying glyph components and sorts them by horizontal position.
Maximum component-height spread and vertical-center spread must each be <= 0.15 * typical_h.
Every adjacent edge-to-edge gap must be >= typical_h, and the largest gap must be <= 1.25 times the smallest gap.

Retention only suppresses the existing thin-band decoration rejection. Top-edge exclusion remains, and a single sufficiently thin connected component spanning >= 90% of the band width still rejects a continuous rule.

concreteFalseCountRisks.risk: Three regularly positioned, glyph-sized scan blotches can satisfy the same bounding-box geometry as actual ornaments.
concreteFalseCountRisks.concreteExample: At typical_h=40, three 15x15 components at x=240,500,760 on the same y level meet the thin, minimum-size, aspect, equal-height, equal-center and 245px-gap guards. Bounding-box checks alone cannot distinguish such blotches from the focused positive fixture's connected stars.
concreteFalseCountRisks.qualification: Static predicate analysis only; no synthetic test or image was run. The existing tiny-speck negative covers 3x3 marks, not this glyph-sized regular-noise case.

concreteFalseCountRisks.risk: A broken thick rule or repeated short dash fragments can be retained if each fragment is compact enough and the gaps are regular.
concreteFalseCountRisks.concreteExample: At typical_h=40, three 28x10 components at x=180,450,720 have height 10 >= 0.25T, width 28 >= 0.2T, height 10 >= 0.35*28, band height 10 < 0.4T, and equal 242px gaps. No individual component spans 90% of their combined 568px band, so the continuous-rule veto does not settle this case.
concreteFalseCountRisks.qualification: Static final-branch risk, not a replay or a claimed end-to-end result. The passed 4px continuous-rule test does not cover compact fragmented rules.

concreteFalseCountRisks.risk: Spacing is evaluated only between qualifying components. Additional undersized or thin ink between them can be ignored, leaving a regular subset that admits a wider noisy band.
concreteFalseCountRisks.qualification: No count/purity check covers all unqualified ink; a long connected rule is still vetoed, but shorter excluded fragments need not be. This is a static limitation, not evidence of extra ink on SOURCE86.
